not_repaired.reason: The defect is in uri_core/tools/fetch_url.py (REFUSED is mapped to one fixed 'private or local network' message). That file is on the permitted list, but both edit attempts were denied by the session's permission settings, which deny the protected uri_core/ directory. Fixing it only in uri_web/safe_fetch.py would be a workaround: it changes W1's SafeFetcher status contract that tests/web relies on, and it still leaves PORT_REFUSED, SCHEME_REFUSED, URL_INVALID and USERINFO_REFUSED mislabeled. I did not bypass the denial with shell edits.

report.notes: Working tree unchanged (git status clean). Proposed fix for fetch_url.py: replace the fixed REFUSED message with a lookup on rec.refusal_code. Private/local message only for ADDRESS_NOT_PUBLIC, ADDRESS_TRANSITION_REFUSED, HOST_LOCAL_NAME, HOST_NUMERIC_AMBIGUOUS, HOST_SINGLE_LABEL. DNS_FAILED and DNS_EMPTY -> 'URI could not reach that URL.' PORT_REFUSED -> a standard-ports (80/443) message. SCHEME_REFUSED -> 'Only http(s) URLs can be fetched.' USERINFO_REFUSED -> a username/password message. URL_INVALID, HOST_INVALID, HOST_MISSING, ADDRESS_INVALID -> an invalid-URL message. Any other code -> 'URI will not fetch that URL.' Keep refusal_code and never include the address. Regression test to add in tests/ssrf/test_ssrf_1_fetch_url.py with tool_with: a resolver raising socket.gaierror for typo-domain-xyz.com expects DNS_FAILED and a message without 'private'/'local'; https://example.com:8443/x expects PORT_REFUSED and a port message. This needs write permission on uri_core/tools/fetch_url.py for the repair session.
